title: Moroccan pre-service elementary teachers: attitudes toward STEM education and mobile devices
venue: International Journal of Evaluation and Research in Education (IJERE)
extended_summary:
This paper examines Moroccan pre-service elementary teachers’ attitudes toward integrated STEM education and toward using mobile devices to support STEM projects in elementary school. The study is motivated by Morocco’s recent curriculum revisions, which introduced integrated STEM education and encouraged ICT/mobile device use in elementary teaching, but require teachers to be prepared and willing to implement these changes.

The authors surveyed 226 Bachelor of Education Elementary Specialty (BEES) students from two Moroccan universities using an online questionnaire. The study focused on second- and third-year pre-service teachers, since first-year students had not yet received the full pedagogy training. The questionnaire measured attitudes toward integrated STEM education and toward mobile devices in that context, and the authors also tested whether attitudes differed by gender, grade level, or pre-university background (scientific vs literary baccalaureate).

Findings showed that participants generally believed integrated STEM education is important, but they lacked confidence in their ability to implement it and were uncertain about how much they would enjoy doing so. In contrast, attitudes toward mobile devices were positive overall, with participants expressing willingness to use them in STEM teaching. Gender and grade level were not associated with attitudes for either topic, but pre-university background mattered for STEM attitudes: students with a scientific baccalaureate were more positive and more confident than those with a literary background. The study concludes that BEES programs should strengthen theoretical and practical preparation for integrated STEM teaching and help future teachers connect content knowledge, pedagogy, and technology.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a single-site correlational survey study using a convenience sample and self-report questionnaire, with Mann-Whitney comparisons but no experimental manipulation. It is peer-reviewed and methodologically transparent, but it does not meet causal-design standards.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports attitudes and readiness rather than observed learning or implementation outcomes, so the practical effect on schooling is indirect and uncertain. Its implications are institutionally relevant for teacher preparation, but the measured impact is modest and not demonstrated empirically.

interventions.use_case: Survey of Moroccan pre-service elementary teachers’ attitudes toward integrated STEM education and the use of mobile devices in STEM teaching; the paper evaluates readiness and perceptions rather than a functioning AI tool.

finding.finding_summary: The paper finds generally positive attitudes toward using mobile devices in integrated STEM education (overall M=3.91/5, n=226). Respondents especially endorsed willingness to use tablets/smartphones to mentor STEM projects and to recommend their use in schools, suggesting perceived usefulness and adoption readiness rather than measured performance gains.
finding.measure: Attitudes toward the use of mobile devices in integrated STEM education (Likert questionnaire; perceived usefulness, ease of use, enjoyment, intention to use)

finding.finding_summary: Attitudes toward integrated STEM education were neutral overall (M=2.92/5, n=226), with teachers agreeing on its importance (M=4.15) but disagreeing on self-confidence to implement it (M=2.08). This suggests positive value beliefs but low readiness and confidence for classroom implementation.
finding.measure: Attitudes toward integrated STEM education; dimensions of importance, enjoyment, and self-confidence (Likert questionnaire)
finding.effect_size: r=0.39 for scientific vs literary baccalaureate difference on overall STEM attitude; other reported comparisons non-significant

finding.finding_summary: The paper identifies a training and curriculum gap in Moroccan elementary teacher preparation: second- and third-year BEES students had no significant differences by grade level in STEM or mobile-device attitudes, implying the program had not yet shifted readiness. The authors recommend adding theoretical courses and practical workshops, and adapting the curriculum to reduce inequities tied to pre-university pathways.
finding.measure: Differences in attitudes by gender, grade level, and pre-university studies; implications for teacher preparation and curriculum design
